report_consistency_checks.qualification: This compares two things your report prints. It is not a finding that a rule was broken.

report_consistency_checks.headline: On entry 1, your report prints Closed as 01/01/2020 and Opened as 01/01/2021, which is the reverse of the expected order. That is a difference between two things your report prints, reported for you to check, and no conclusion is drawn from it.

jurisdiction.label: Nova Scotia
jurisdiction.citation: Limitation of Actions Act, S.N.S. 2014, c. 35, s. 8(1)
jurisdiction.operative_words: a claim ... may not be brought after the earlier of (a) two years from the day on which the claim is discovered; and (b) fifteen years from the day on which the act or omission on which the claim is based occurred

withheld.plain: This entry does not print an outstanding amount, amount past due, collection, charge-off or default claim, so the court time limit was not applied to it.
withheld.missing_prerequisite: a printed indicator of an outstanding claim (an amount past due, a collection or charge-off action, or a default status)

performed.label: a month the report rates as a bad debt while the same month says the account was paid or closed without a derogatory rating
benign_explanations_considered: a status can change inside one month, so both statements may be partly true
a code meaning is quoted exactly as the report prints it in its own legend, never decoded by this build
performed.plain: No month of any account read here has an adverse rating and a non-derogatory narrative at the same time.

performed.label: a payment amount and a no-payment description printed for the same month
benign_explanations_considered: a payment can be posted and later reversed, and a row may report the month a payment was applied rather than received
a write-off is an accounting event and does not by itself stop a payment being recorded
performed.plain: No month of an account read here prints both a payment amount and an explicit no-payment description.

performed.label: a first-delinquency date printed later than a month the same account already shows as late
benign_explanations_considered: an unknown rating (X) and a blank cell are never treated as a late month
a rating of 1 or 0 is a paid-as-agreed month and is not late
the anchor may describe the current delinquency rather than the first one, which the report does not say
performed.plain: No account read here prints a first-delinquency date later than a month its own history already shows as late.

withheld_candidates.reason: A creditor can close an account and then write it off or place it for collection, and a closed account normally keeps reporting its final state. The printed closure date is therefore not evidence that a later event is wrong.
withheld_candidates.missing_prerequisite: a report statement tying the later event to a date before the closure

withheld_candidates.reason: Closure does not require a zero balance: an account can be closed with a balance outstanding, so a closed account with a balance is ordinary.
withheld_candidates.missing_prerequisite: a printed statement that the balance was paid at closure

withheld_candidates.reason: A collection placement or a transfer does not by itself refresh or change the delinquency the account already shows, and the report prints no re-aged anchor.
withheld_candidates.missing_prerequisite: two comparable printed delinquency anchors for the same account

withheld_candidates.reason: The printed 30/60/90/#M figures are cumulative lifetime counts while the visible table is a short window; the two are not comparable, so no comparison is made and no conclusion is drawn from their difference.
withheld_candidates.missing_prerequisite: a printed statement of the period the counts cover

withheld_candidates.reason: An unknown rating (X), a blank cell and an unprinted month are not missed payments and are never counted as one.
withheld_candidates.missing_prerequisite: a printed meaning for the unknown rating

withheld_candidates.reason: The product type OPEN describes the kind of account, not whether it is still open, so it is never read as a lifecycle status.
withheld_candidates.missing_prerequisite: a printed closure date or a closure narrative

withheld_candidates.reason: Comparable evidence for this candidate exists only when the consumer owns two reports of the same account. The owned report history and its comparison view supply that evidence; it is never inferred from one snapshot, and the snapshot association must be shown before the candidate is raised.
withheld_candidates.missing_prerequisite: two owned results for the same account whose printed debt identifiers match

legal_dependencies.note: a security freeze is a disclosure restriction, not automatically a mandatory printed notation; whether the consumer placed one is not printed on the report

detected_report_information.label: a consumer dispute notation
detected_report_information.detail: We did not detect a consumer dispute notation in the information we could read. Absence of a keyword does not prove the feature is absent or that any obligation was breached.

legal_dependencies.proposition: a consumer reporting agency shall note in a subsequent report that a consumer notified the agency that information is disputed
legal_dependencies.condition: the consumer's actual notification of a dispute to the agency
legal_dependencies.note: a dispute keyword on the report does not itself prove the notification required by § 1681c(f); whether the notification was made is not printed on the report

common_errors.label: an account with contradictory dates
common_errors.detail: This report prints at least one account whose opened date is later than its closed date. The printed dates conflict.

common_error_checklist.description: A debt may stay on your report after the deadline to sue has passed. These are two separate time limits.

issues.explanation: This report prints SPRUCE FICTION BANK with an opened date later than its closed date (2021-01-01 after 2020-01-01).
issues.uncertainty: The dates conflict. The report does not show which date needs correction, and a later correction may explain the difference.

rule_assessment.requirement: An account cannot close before it opened.

assessment.plain: We reviewed your report against the common-error checklist using the report facts available for each applicable check.

qualifications: These checks read your report. A violation is shown when report evidence supports a breach of a defined reporting rule or requirement.
Only the checks named below were run against your report.
No check of every possible legal issue was made, and none is implied.

We have tested this service on five report layouts: one Equifax Canada consumer specimen admitted by digest, one TransUnion Canada consumer disclosure admitted by a measured structural contract, one Equifax Australia consumer credit file, one Experian United States consumer-disclosure format family, one Experian United Kingdom consumer format family evidenced by structure from a single captured consumer report example of a recorded vintage. The US and Australia examples are dated 2015 and 2016; the UK Experian example is dated 2007. These examples do not certify every current report layout. We also read recognizable bureau reports in a general way, including the supported UK TransUnion consumer fields. We then use the facts we can read. If a document is not a credit report, or we cannot read it, we say which of the two it is and what to do next.
A check can also be reported as not applicable to your report, or as unresolved. Neither one ran, and neither one passed.
A report-data rule can support a violation from source-linked report facts. An applicable statute may provide additional context.
Each finding states the supporting report evidence and any specific uncertainty.
A date comparison is arithmetic. On its own it does not show that anything was reported unlawfully.
